subject.title: Control UI: Config upgrade/hardening suggestions should apply changes automatically with before/after diff and user acceptance, not direct users to edit files manually

question: Which Control UI security/auth recommendations may be applied automatically, and what confirmation, audit, restart, and allowlist policy must wrap those config.patch writes?
rationale: The source shows the primitive exists, but deciding when the UI may turn hardening advice into an executable config change is a product/security boundary rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Allowlisted recommendation actions
options.body: Permit a narrow set of maintainer-approved recommendations to propose config.patch changes with before/after diff, explicit acceptance, audit note, and restart messaging.

options.title: Manual guidance only
options.body: Keep security-sensitive recommendations as docs and copyable config snippets, accepting the current support burden and UX friction.

options.title: Defer to broader protected-config flow
options.body: Wait for the protected config approval work to define a shared policy before adding Control UI-specific apply actions.

recommendation.title: Allowlisted recommendation actions
recommendation.body: Permit a narrow set of maintainer-approved recommendations to propose config.patch changes with before/after diff, explicit acceptance, audit note, and restart messaging.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses recent Control UI, config safety, and security-auth behavior where steipete has the strongest observed history signal.
